title: `VAR_POP` and `STDDEV_POP` of one value are 0, even for NaN or ±inf
verdict: 0 for any single value; the reference gives NaN for a non-finite one
description: The finalize of `VarPopOperation` and `STDDevPopOperation` is `count > 1 ? dsquared / count : 0` (and its square root): a group or frame with exactly one non-NULL value gives 0 whatever the value is. So `VAR_POP` and `STDDEV_POP` of `[NaN]`, of `[NULL, NaN]` and of `[inf]` are 0.0, as an aggregate, as a window over a frame, and as `list_var_pop`. Reported upstream as DD-3 (duckdb#28329, fix duckdb#28344 open).

Two values or more go through Welford's update and give NaN for a NaN or ±inf among them (duckdb-nonfinite-aggregates): `[NaN, NaN]` and `[NaN, 1]` are NaN. `VAR_SAMP` and `STDDEV_SAMP` of one value are NULL. `COVAR_POP` of one pair with a NaN is NaN: the covariance has no such special case.

sverify's grouped `VAR_*`/`STDDEV_*` return NaN when a value is NaN (`COUNT(isnan(x)) > 0`, the handling of DD-3), so the grouped plan gives the reference's NaN. The window form (`window_var`) wrote `VAR_POP(x) OVER (...)` without that guard, so a frame whose only value is NaN gave 0.0 through the written plan; #758 adds the guard. A ±inf does not reach either: the plan raises its domain error first (`MAX(ABS(x)) = inf`).
The docs are silent on one value: a docs gap (duckdb-var-stddev).
reference: `varOf` (`core/Sverify/Core/Aggregate.lean`, D30): NaN for a NaN or an infinity among the values, 0 for one finite value. The DuckDB profile's `stat_algo` row `WELFORD_CHAN` claims `StatProps` (`core/Sverify/Core/StatProps.lean`, `varStat`), which outside finite values asks for the reference's own value, NaN; the writer's NaN guard is what keeps DuckDB inside it: the shim `nan_through` of Profile.duckdb's `agg.var` `stat_algo` row, proved by `Stat.nanGuard_varStat` (`core/Sverify/Core/StatProps.lean`). Found again by #758 (`test_engines_agree[rolling variance (rows)]`): Polars, before its refusal of windowed variances, gave NaN for a frame of `[NULL, NaN]`, and DuckDB 0.0 through both the written plan and Ibis's own SQL.

evidence.note: VarPopOperation: `target = state.count > 1 ? (state.dsquared / state.count) : 0;` STDDevPopOperation: `state.count > 1 ? sqrt(state.dsquared / state.count) : 0`

evidence.sql: SELECT var_pop(x), stddev_pop(x), var_samp(x), stddev_samp(x) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE)) t(x)
SELECT var_pop(x), stddev_pop(x), var_samp(x) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE), (NULL)) t(x)
SELECT var_pop(x), stddev_pop(x), var_samp(x) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE), ('nan'::DOUBLE)) t(x)
SELECT covar_pop(x, y), covar_samp(x, y), corr(x, y) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE, 1.0::DOUBLE)) t(x, y)
SELECT var_pop(x) OVER (ORDER BY i ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM (VALUES (1, NULL::DOUBLE), (2, 'nan'::DOUBLE), (3, 1.0::DOUBLE)) t(i, x)

evidence.note: test_var_pop_of_one_nan: the case `rolling variance (rows)` on t.amount = [NULL, NaN], through the written plan on DuckDB and Ibis's own SQL; both give 0.0 at the second row

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (streaming engine) gives NaN for `var(ddof=0)` and `std(ddof=0)` of `[NULL, NaN]` and of `[NaN]`, as the reference does.
